question: Citation graph is a good tool to find relevant work and to help understand the evolution of the domain. What recent research has been done to analyze scientific discourse and generate citation content using citation networks and related textual information?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer must frame recent research as addressing enhancement of excitation and collection of emission from single fluorescent reporters and signal generation in the presence of noise sources.
examples: research has focused on enhancing excitation of single fluorescent reporters and collecting their emission
generating observable signals from single fluorophores despite noise sources
excitation enhancement, efficient emission collection, and noise rejection

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer must identify TIRF microscopy as achieving single-fluorophore resolution using high-NA oil-immersion objectives and EM-CCD cameras with over 30x signal-to-noise improvement.
examples: TIRF microscopy achieves single fluorophore resolution with high NA oil objectives
EM-CCD cameras provide over a 30x increase in signal-to-noise ratio

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer must mention quantum dot advances such as multi-color and 3D single-particle tracking and in vivo tracking with molecular-level resolution.
examples: multi-color and 3D QD tracking reveal cell signaling mechanisms
QD tracking in vivo observes processes at molecular resolution in whole animals

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer must state that plasmonic nanostructures (e.g., bowtie nanoantennas) locally enhance excitation fields, yielding fluorescence enhancement factors of roughly 100 to 1000, including the 1340x bowtie result.
examples: plasmonic nanostructures enhance local field excitation intensity
fluorescence enhancement factor from ~100 to ~1000
gold bowtie nanoantennas enhance single-molecule fluorescence by up to a factor of 1,340

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: The answer must synthesize plasmonic drawbacks against dielectric alternatives: non-radiative metal losses and quenching, low photon directionality, geometry/material-fixed resonance, versus dielectric high-Q mismatch with spectrally broad room-temperature emitters, and hot-spot sparsity versus high enhancement.
examples: intrinsic metal losses cause non-radiative decay and quenching
resonance wavelength fixed by size, shape, and material
high-Q modes versus inhomogeneously broadened emission
1000x enhancement comes at the cost of sparse localized hot spots

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer must note that dielectric optical microcavities achieved only modest emission rate enhancements, with high-Q resonances mismatching broad emitter spectra at room temperature.
examples: early dielectric microcavities show modest emission rate enhancement
high-Q cavity modes mismatch spectrally wide emission of inhomogeneously broadened emitters

ingredients.name: answer_critical_5
ingredients.criterion: The answer must describe recent plasmonic-dielectric hybrid nano-gap and dielectric nanowire-slab structures achieving ~1000x enhancement but with highly localized hot spots covering only a small fraction of the surface.
examples: plasmonic-dielectric hybrid nano-gaps reach ~1000x enhancement
hot spots sparsely occupy only a small fraction of total surface area

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer may cite film-coupled metal nanocube systems achieving >1000x spontaneous emission enhancement while maintaining >0.5 quantum efficiency and 84% directional collection, satisfying practical device requirements (directional emission, room-temperature broadband operation).
examples: spontaneous emission rate enhancements exceeding 1,000
84% collection efficiency with high quantum efficiency maintained

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer may note that dipole emitter orientation in nanogaps is vital, with angle-resolved measurements combined with full-wave simulations predicting time-resolved emission.
examples: angle-resolved fluorescence determines emission dipole orientation
3D dipole distributions in simulations match experiments

ingredients.name: valuable_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer must conclude that the highest enhancement factors require precise alignment between emitters and cavity modes, achieved through sophisticated nanofabrication.
examples: precise emitter-cavity mode alignment is required
sophisticated nanofabrication underpins high enhancement factors
